languages.$comment: Language registry. 'active' = shipped in the UI, in this order. Deferred languages are listed so IDs/codes are reserved; they get full feature blocks when activated. Variants (e.g. pt-BR) are added later as separate entries with "extends": "pt" and only the files/entries that differ. See docs/DATA_FORMAT.md §Languages.

ru.name: Russian
ru.variantNote: Standard Russian; stress marks (U+0301) on every polysyllabic word; always write ё

noun.note: gen = genitive singular (genitive plural for pluralia tantum); pl = nominative plural when it exists; f = feminine counterpart of a person noun (учитель → учительница)

verb.note: aspect: ipf|pf|bi; pair = aspect partner; 1sg/2sg/3pl = present (ipf) or simple future (pf); past = 'm, f' only when stress shifts or stem is irregular

adj.note: comp only when irregular; short = short forms 'm, f' when commonly used

sr.name: Serbian
sr.variantNote: Ekavian standard of Serbia. Stored in Cyrillic; Latin is derived by rule at runtime

noun.note: gen = genitive singular; pl = nominative plural; f = feminine counterpart of a person noun (учитељ → учитељица)

verb.note: lpt = active past participle 'm, f' (радио, радила)

ja.name: Japanese
ja.variantNote: Standard Japanese; usual written form (kanji where customary, kana where customary)

noun.note: pl whenever a plural exists; gen only when not trivially -(e)s; f = feminine counterpart of a person noun (Lehrer → Lehrerin)

verb.note: pp includes the auxiliary: 'hat gegessen', 'ist gegangen'

noun.note: pl only when irregular; f = feminine counterpart of a person noun (profesor → profesora)
pl only when irregular (-ões, -ães, -is…); f = feminine counterpart of a person noun (professor → professora)
gen = genitive singular; pl = nominative plural; f = feminine counterpart of a person noun (nauczyciel → nauczycielka)

verb.note: haeyo = polite present (가요); past = polite past (갔어요)

noun.note: pl whenever it exists; dim = diminutive when common; f = feminine counterpart of a person noun (leraar → lerares)

verb.note: past = 'sg, pl'; pp includes auxiliary: 'heeft gegeten', 'is gegaan'

noun.note: pl only when irregular; f = feminine counterpart for people/animals

adj.note: f when it differs; pl when irregular

hy.name: Armenian
hy.variantNote: Eastern Armenian, reformed (Soviet) orthography, as used in Armenia

noun.note: acc shows consonant mutation and harmony (kitabı)
gen = genitive singular; pl = nominative plural; f = feminine counterpart of a person noun (δάσκαλος → δασκάλα)

verb.note: lemma is 1sg present; aor = simple past 1sg (έγραψα); fut = 'θα γράψω'

fields.$comment: Field table shown in step 4, in this order. placements: subset of off|front|back|on|word. 'side': learning = describes the learned word (always moved to the back of reverse cards); known = in the user's language; concept = language-neutral. 'langs': learning languages for which the row is shown ('*' = all active). 'modes': bilingual|same. Defaults may differ per learning language via 'defaultByLang'. 'more': the row is under "More…", closed by default.

fields.label: Word
fields.help: The word you are learning. Always on the question side of forward cards.

fields.label: Translation
fields.help: The word in your language, with a short hint when your language uses one word for several meanings. In same-language mode this is a short definition.

fields.label: Gender / article
fields.help: Shows the article (der Tisch, la mesa) or a gender mark (m/f/n) next to the word.

fields.label: Stress marks
fields.help: Marks the stressed vowel (молоко́). Applies to the word, its forms and the highlighted word in examples.

fields.label: Reading (furigana)
fields.help: Kana reading above the kanji. Also controls furigana in example sentences.

fields.label: Romanization
fields.help: The word in Latin letters: Hepburn (Japanese), pinyin (Chinese), Revised Romanization (Korean), transliteration (Russian, Armenian, Greek). For Chinese it also controls pinyin in example sentences.

fields.label: Other script
fields.help: Shows the word in the other Serbian script (Latin if the deck uses Cyrillic, and vice versa).

fields.label: Measure word / counter
fields.help: The classifier used when counting this noun (一本书, 鉛筆を三本).

fields.label: Hanja
fields.help: Chinese characters behind Sino-Korean words (은행 → 銀行). Shown only for words that have them.

fields.label: Key forms
fields.help: The few forms you need to use the word: plural, genitive, past tense, aspect partner, verb class… not full tables.

fields.label: IPA
fields.help: Pronunciation in the International Phonetic Alphabet.

fields.label: Examples
fields.help: Example sentences with the word highlighted. Use the slider to choose how many (0–3).

fields.label: Example translations
fields.help: Shows each example in your language when a matching translation exists. Some examples are written natively and have no translation.

fields.label: Antonyms & related
fields.help: Opposites and closely related words, in the language you are learning.

fields.label: Register
fields.help: Marks informal, formal, vulgar or offensive words.

fields.label: Emoji
fields.help: A picture hint for concrete words (💧 water). Most abstract words have none.

fields.label: Concept ID
fields.help: A tiny code at the bottom of the card (e.g. word-water). If you find a mistake while studying in Anki, include this code in your report so we can find the exact entry.

deckOptions.label: Reverse cards
deckOptions.help: Adds a second card per word: your language → the language you learn. On reverse cards everything about the learned word moves to the answer side so nothing gives the answer away.

deckOptions.label: Type the answer
deckOptions.help: On reverse cards you type the word instead of just recalling it. Anki compares your spelling with the main form (articles included, stress marks ignored).

deckOptions.label: Serbian script
deckOptions.help: Serbian is written in both Cyrillic and Latin. Choose the one used on your cards.

labels.$comment: Card labels, shown in the KNOWN language (the language the user speaks). 'en' is the master key set; every other active language must have the same keys (generation unit labels:<code>). Missing languages fall back to 'en' at runtime. Keep labels short: they sit in small grey captions on cards.

version.$comment: Bump 'data' on every data release (YYYY.MM.DD[.n]). The app shows it in the footer and attaches it to feedback reports.
